title: AgentExecutionRequest
description: POST /v1/agent-executions, control plane to agent runtime (ADR-0004 §11). One call, exactly one node attempt. The runtime never selects the next node, never decides to retry, never branches and never schedules work; all workflow control lives in the graph engine.

protocolVersion.description: Incompatible versions fail fast at startup rather than at the first interesting node.

agentVersionHash.description: The exact Agent definition to execute, taken from GraphRun.agentPins (ADR-0022 §3). Naming the version rather than only the agent is what makes the execution record reproducible and what stops an agent edit from changing an in-flight run.

instructions.description: Platform-authored instruction blocks. ADR-0004 Security Impact: untrusted content must never be placed here. Repository, issue and page content reaches the model through the context bundle, as data.

contextBundleRef.description: Fetched by reference via GET /v1/context-bundles/{ref}, not inlined. Costs a round trip per node attempt; keeps the request small and the bundle content-addressed.

tools.description: Descriptors only — no implementations, no endpoints, no credentials. The runtime cannot invoke a tool except through the callback.

maxRetrievals.description: ADR-0027 §3. Bounds context.search calls per node attempt. Exhausting it does not fail the node — the tool reports the bound was reached and the agent proceeds with what it has, because converting a bounded resource into a run failure is worse than a slightly thinner bundle.

callbackToken.description: Bound to (runId, nodeId, iteration, attempt) and valid until the attempt deadline. ADR-0004 §10: this token is the bearer of the capability grant — the tool layer resolves the grant from the token, so the runtime cannot widen its own authority by asking differently. Single-attempt; a retry gets a new token and a new grant.
